assumptions: The ticket asks for a minimal but runnable FastAPI application in a single Python file named main.py, plus the minimum supporting files (requirements.txt, README) to run it.
Python 3.10+ is the target runtime and the app is served with uvicorn.

Since no domain was specified, the API exposes a simple in-memory CRUD resource called 'items' (id, name, description, price) alongside a health-check endpoint, so the script demonstrates GET/POST/PUT/DELETE without needing a database.
No database, authentication, Docker, or deployment configuration is required; data is stored in a module-level Python dict and resets on restart.
Pydantic v2 is used for request/response models.
Tests are optional but a single smoke test with FastAPI's TestClient is included to prove the endpoints work; no test framework beyond pytest is introduced.
The project lives at the repository root (no src/ package layout) to keep it 'simple' as requested.

tasks.description: Create project files at repo root: main.py, requirements.txt, README.md, and .gitignore (ignore __pycache__/, .venv/, *.pyc, .pytest_cache/).
In requirements.txt pin the runtime deps: fastapi>=0.110, uvicorn[standard]>=0.27, pydantic>=2.6, and dev dep pytest>=8.0 and httpx>=0.27 (needed by TestClient).

In main.py, add imports (typing, fastapi: FastAPI, HTTPException, status; pydantic: BaseModel, Field) and instantiate the app: app = FastAPI(title="Simple FastAPI Example", version="1.0.0", description="A minimal FastAPI service with an in-memory items resource.").

Define Pydantic v2 models in main.py: ItemCreate(name: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=100), description: str | None = None, price: float = Field(gt=0)); ItemUpdate with all fields optional (name, description, price); Item(ItemCreate) adding id: int.

Add module-level in-memory storage in main.py: _items: dict[int, Item] = {} and _next_id counter starting at 1, plus a small helper _get_item_or_404(item_id: int) -> Item that raises HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found") when missing.
Implement GET / returning {"message": "Welcome to the Simple FastAPI API", "docs": "/docs"} and GET /health returning {"status": "ok"} with status_code 200.
Implement GET /items returning list[Item] of all stored items, with optional query params skip: int = 0 and limit: int = 10 applied to the list for basic pagination.
Implement GET /items/{item_id} returning Item, using _get_item_or_404 so an unknown id yields HTTP 404 with a JSON detail message.
Implement POST /items accepting ItemCreate, assigning the next auto-increment id, storing the Item, and returning it with response_model=Item and status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED.

Implement PUT /items/{item_id} accepting ItemUpdate, applying only the fields present via model_dump(exclude_unset=True) onto the existing item (404 if absent), storing and returning the updated Item.
Implement DELETE /items/{item_id} that 404s when the id is unknown, otherwise removes it from _items and returns status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT with no body.
At the bottom of main.py add an entrypoint guard: if __name__ == "__main__": import uvicorn; uvicorn.run("main:app", host="127.0.0.1", port=8000, reload=True).
Add docstrings/summary+description arguments to each route decorator so the auto-generated OpenAPI docs at /docs and /redoc are self-explanatory.

Create test_main.py with pytest tests using fastapi.testclient.TestClient covering: GET /health returns 200 {"status":"ok"}; POST /items returns 201 and an id; GET /items/{id} returns the created item; PUT updates a field; DELETE returns 204 and a subsequent GET returns 404. Reset _items and the id counter between tests with a pytest fixture (autouse=True).

Write README.md with: project description, setup steps (python -m venv .venv, activate, pip install -r requirements.txt), run command (uvicorn main:app --reload), URLs for /docs and /redoc, example curl commands for each endpoint, how to run tests (pytest), and a note that data is in-memory and resets on restart.
Verify end-to-end locally: install deps, run pytest (all tests pass), start uvicorn main:app --reload, and confirm http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs loads and a POST then GET of an item works.
